# Mono-Black Midrange

- **Format:** Casual 60-card, 1v1
- **Archetype:** Mono-black midrange: kill nearly everything, draw extra cards, win with a few bombs, two planeswalkers and big Gray Merchant drains
- **Played by:** either — suits whoever enjoys long, patient games and deciding what to kill; a good deck to hand to whoever is playing a stronger opponent
- **Status:** idea
- **Complexity:** 3/5
- **Estimated power:** 6.5 with owned cards only, 7.5 with the buys (on a 1v1 scale)
- **Configuration:** **Standalone strongest deck** (for games against stronger opponents). It borrows from other decks, as listed under Shared-pool conflicts.

Mono-Black Midrange is the "answer everything" deck. It kills almost every creature the opponent plays and draws extra cards along the way. Then it wins with a few huge threats (Grave Titan, Desecration Demon, Massacre Wurm, and the planeswalkers Ob Nixilis and Liliana) and big Gray Merchant life drains. It suits a patient player who likes long games and working out which threat to kill, and it's the deck to reach for against a stronger opponent.

### Why these buys (in priority order)

1. **2x Murderous Rider // Swift End** (replaces Tribute to Hunger, Withering Torment). Two cards in one. Swift End is a 3-mana instant that destroys any creature or planeswalker (you lose 2 life). The card then goes on an adventure (exile), and later you can cast it from there as a 2/3 lifelink creature. The cheapest real upgrade in the list. *Also useful in: Mono-B Zombies 60 (it's a Zombie Knight), Orzhov decks, Gisa Commander (on 19% of EDHREC Gisa decks).*
2. **1x Ob Nixilis Reignited** (replaces Bloodtithe Collector). A 5-mana planeswalker with 5 loyalty. +1: you draw a card and lose 1 life. −3: destroy a creature. In 1v1 it takes over games if it isn't attacked down quickly. *Also useful in: Gisa Commander, any black control deck (Dimir/Orzhov).*
3. **1x Liliana, Death's Majesty** (replaces God-Eternal Bontu). A 5-mana planeswalker with 5 loyalty. +1 makes a 2/2 Zombie every turn (and mills two cards), so she makes her own blockers. −3 puts a creature card from your graveyard onto the battlefield: Grave Titan, Massacre Wurm, or a second Gray Merchant drain or Chupacabra kill. Bontu's enter trigger needs spare permanents to sacrifice, and this deck rarely has any. Same price as Ob Nixilis. *Also useful in: Gisa Commander (on 27% of EDHREC Gisa decks; it's already a buy in the Gisa target list, so buy 2 if both decks will be built at once), Mono-B Zombies 60.*
4. **3x Infernal Grasp** (replaces Feed the Swarm, Eaten Alive, Sign in Blood). A 2-mana instant that destroys any creature (you lose 2 life), including artifact creatures that Go for the Throat can't touch. Cheap, fast and unconditional, which is the best kind of removal. *Also useful in: Every black 60-card deck (Zombies, Vampires, Orzhov, Dimir), Gisa Commander (on 23% of EDHREC Gisa decks).*
5. **4x Gifted Aetherborn** (replaces Mire Triton, Knight of Malice, Nullpriest of Oblivion, Gatekeeper of Malakir). The best 2-drop for this deck. A 2/3 with deathtouch and lifelink: it survives 1–2 power attackers, trades with anything bigger, and gains back early damage. The owned list's 2-drops are its weakest slots. *Also useful in: Orzhov Vampires 60 (it's a Vampire), Gisa Commander.*
6. **2x Ravenous Chupacabra** (replaces Deadly Plot, Tendrils of Corruption). 4 mana: destroy an opponent's creature and keep a 2/2 body. The same cost as the owned kill spells, but it leaves a creature behind (at sorcery speed). *Also useful in: Any black deck, Gisa Commander.*
7. **2x Vampire Nighthawk** (replaces Ayara, First of Locthwain; Fleshbag Marauder). Brings it to 3 copies. A 3-mana 2/3 flyer with deathtouch and lifelink: it blocks flyers, wins races and adds 2 devotion for Gray Merchant. *Also useful in: Orzhov Vampires 60, Gisa Commander.*
8. **1x Gray Merchant of Asphodel** (replaces Liliana's Reaver). A second big drain finisher; it usually drains 3–5 (a 6–10 point life swing) in this all-black deck. Reprinted in FDC 2026 (2 Oct 2026); MTGMate already stocks it at reprint prices, so there's no need to wait. Both copies are used in this deck, so the Gisa Commander deck (which also runs Gary) needs a third copy if both are built at the same time. *Also useful in: Mono-B Zombies 60 (it's a Zombie), Gisa Commander (on 66% of EDHREC Gisa decks).*

| 3 Infernal Grasp | Feed the Swarm; Eaten Alive; Sign in Blood | **Small–moderate.** Feed the Swarm is sorcery-speed and costs life equal to the target's mana value. Eaten Alive needs a creature to sacrifice, or 5 mana in total. Sign in Blood is card draw, not removal. |
| 1 Gray Merchant of Asphodel (#2) | Liliana's Reaver | **Small.** Reaver is a strong 4-drop (4/3 deathtouch; when it deals combat damage to a player they discard and you get a 2/2 Zombie). You lose a second game-ending drain. |
| 1 Ob Nixilis Reignited | Bloodtithe Collector | **Moderate.** Collector is a 3/4 flyer whose discard only works if the opponent already lost life that turn. Ob Nixilis draws a card every turn or kills a creature. |
| 1 Liliana, Death's Majesty | God-Eternal Bontu | **Small–moderate.** Bontu is a 5/6 menace whose enter trigger trades spare permanents for cards. You lose a planeswalker that makes a 2/2 blocker every turn and brings back Grave Titan or Gray Merchant. |

Sideboard: the owned list's sideboard swaps in Stab, Soul-Guide Lantern, Sorcerous Spyglass and Vampire Spawn for Withering Torment, Feed the Swarm, Tribute to Hunger and Knight of Malice. Those four are in the owned list's main deck instead.

Overall: the owned list plays at about **6.5** (focused and tuned, with bombs and ~13 removal). The target list plays at about **7.5**, with cheaper removal, more 2-for-1s, two planeswalkers and a much better early game.

## Notes

### Game plan (in plain words)

You're the control-ish deck. Your job is to **survive the early turns, kill everything important, and win late with cards your opponent can't match.**

- **Turns 1–3:** play a sturdy early creature (Gifted Aetherborn, Vampire Nighthawk). Use cheap **removal** (spells that destroy a creature, e.g. Infernal Grasp, Go for the Throat) on their best creature. Draw extra cards with Night's Whisper.
- **Turns 4–5:** play creatures that bring a bonus. Ravenous Chupacabra and Murderous Rider kill something *and* leave a body. That's a **2-for-1**: one of your cards dealt with one of theirs and still left you something. Desecration Demon (a 6/6 flyer for 4) also lands here.
- **Turns 5–6+:** land a bomb: Grave Titan, Massacre Wurm, or a planeswalker (Ob Nixilis, Liliana). Then finish with **Gray Merchant of Asphodel**. When it enters, the opponent loses life equal to your **devotion to black** (count every {B} symbol in the mana costs of your permanents on the battlefield, including Gary's own two and your planeswalkers'), and you gain that much.

Jargon used on these cards:
- **Instant:** you can cast it on the opponent's turn.
- **Deathtouch:** any damage it deals to a creature destroys it.
- **Lifelink:** its damage also gains you that much life.
- **Menace:** it can't be blocked except by two or more creatures.
- **Edict** (Tribute to Hunger; in the owned list also Gatekeeper of Malakir and Fleshbag Marauder): the opponent sacrifices a creature *of their choice*. It gets around creatures that can't be targeted. Consumed by Greed is a stronger version: they must sacrifice the creature with the **greatest power** they control.

### Opening hand and mulligans

- **Keep:** 2–4 lands, plus at least one thing to do on turns 2–3 (a 2- or 3-mana creature, a removal spell or Night's Whisper). Three lands and a mix of cheap spells is ideal.
- **Mulligan:**
  - 0–1 lands.
  - 5 or more lands with no card draw.
  - 2 lands where every spell costs 5–6 (especially when you go first, because you don't get the extra draw).
- **How to mulligan (London mulligan):** shuffle, draw a new 7, then put 1 card on the bottom for each mulligan you've taken.
- The deck has 24 lands. About 84% of opening sevens have 2–5 lands, so most hands are keepable.

### Play tips

1. **Don't fire removal at the first thing you see.**
   - Kill the creatures that take over games: flyers, "lords" that pump a team, and anything that draws cards or makes tokens.
   - Plain small creatures can just be blocked by Aetherborn or Nighthawk.
2. **Use instants on their turn.** Passing with 2–3 mana open lets you kill an attacker mid-combat or at the end of their turn. Night's Whisper and Sign in Blood are sorceries, so cast them on your own turn.
3. **Watch your life total.**
   - These all cost life: Night's Whisper (2), Infernal Grasp (2), Swift End (2), Phyrexian Arena (1 every turn), Ob Nixilis's +1 (1), Midnight Reaper (1 each time one of your non-token creatures dies) and Castle Locthwain's draw (1 per card in your hand afterwards). In the owned list, also Sign in Blood, Withering Torment and Feed the Swarm.
   - Against fast decks, play blockers first and draw cards later.
   - Lifelink creatures and Gray Merchant refill your life.
4. **Order matters.**
   - Play Kalitas *before* your removal. While he's out, their non-token creatures that would die are exiled instead, and you get a 2/2 Zombie each time.
   - Play Gray Merchant after other black permanents are down, for a bigger drain.
   - Desecration Demon: at the start of every combat (yours and theirs), the opponent may sacrifice a creature to tap it. Kill their small creatures first so they run out of creatures to sacrifice.
5. **Two special card types.**
   - **Murderous Rider is an "Adventure" card.** Cast the instant half (Swift End) to kill something. The card then goes to exile ("on an adventure"), and later you can cast the 2/3 lifelink Rider from exile. When the Rider dies it goes to the bottom of your library, not your graveyard.
   - **Ob Nixilis and Liliana are planeswalkers.** Each enters with 5 loyalty. Use one ability per turn, on your own turn, when you could cast a sorcery.
     - Ob Nixilis: +1 you draw a card and lose 1 life; −3 destroys a creature.
     - Liliana: +1 makes a 2/2 Zombie and mills your top two cards; −3 returns a creature card from your graveyard to the battlefield. Best targets: Grave Titan, Massacre Wurm, Gray Merchant (a second drain) or Ravenous Chupacabra (a second kill).
     - The opponent can attack planeswalkers, so keep a blocker around. Liliana's Zombies do that job.

Small rules notes:
- Midnight Reaper: whenever one of your non-token creatures dies (including the Reaper itself), it deals 1 damage to you and you draw a card, so trading in combat is fine.
- God-Eternal Bontu (owned list): when she enters, you may sacrifice spare permanents (Zombie tokens, or extra lands late) and draw that many cards.
- Consuming Corruption counts Swamps. Witch's Cottage counts; Castle Locthwain and Memorial to Folly don't.

### Watch out for (opponent's cards)

- **Board wipes:** Day of Judgment, Austere Command and Sunblast Angel (destroys all tapped creatures) in the Angels precon, plus Wrath-style cards from an experienced player. Don't dump your whole hand. Two or three threats at a time is enough, because your removal does the rest.
- **Counterspells** (Izzet, or any blue deck). Bait with a cheaper spell first, or cast two spells in one turn. Bring in Duress.
- **Creatures your "destroy" spells can't hit:**
  - Hexproof or protection from black: use edicts (Tribute to Hunger, Consumed by Greed; Gatekeeper and Fleshbag in the owned list).
  - Indestructible: use exile (Eaten Alive) or −X/−X (Moment of Craving, Mutilate).
  - Artifact creatures: Go for the Throat can't target them, so use Grasp or Hero's Downfall.
- **Big lifelink flyers** like Lyra Dawnbringer, and cheap exile like Swords to Plowshares aimed at your Titan or Demon. Save Hero's Downfall or Grasp for Lyra, and don't rely on a single threat.

### Matchups

- **vs Angels (white flyers + lifegain):**
  - Aetherborn can't block flyers, but Nighthawk can.
  - Massacre Wurm gives −2/−2, so it only kills creatures with toughness 2 or less: Giada, Inspiring Overseer, Angel of Vitality (while they're under 25 life) and Spirit tokens. It does **not** kill 3-toughness angels (Dazzling Angel, Youthful Valkyrie, Serra Avenger) or anything Giada has grown with +1/+1 counters.
  - Save kill spells for Lyra, Archangel of Tithes and Righteous Valkyrie.
  - Their removal: Swords to Plowshares, Fateful Absence, Devout Decree (exiles a black creature) and Valorous Stance (destroys a creature with toughness 4 or more: Titan, Demon, Wurm, Kalitas, Josu). Stasis Snare and Grasp of Fate are enchantments: destroy them with Withering Torment or Feed the Swarm (sideboard) and your creature comes back.
- **vs Zombies (go-wide):**
  - Kill Death Baron and the other lords first.
  - Once the lords are gone, Massacre Wurm is a blowout: their 2/2s all die and each one costs them 2 life.
- **vs Izzet (burn + counters):**
  - Kill prowess creatures on sight.
  - Lifelink matters here; don't fall low from your own card draw.
- **vs Gruul (ramp + big creatures):**
  - Kill mana elves early (Consuming Corruption, Grasp).
  - Save Hero's Downfall for the big stuff.
- **vs stronger opponents:** play game 1 with the main deck, then sideboard based on what you saw.

### Sideboard guide (target list; always swap one-for-one so you stay at 60)

- **Fast or go-wide creature decks (Zombies, Rabbits, tokens):**
  - In: Mutilate, 2 Moment of Craving, Seeker's Folly.
  - Out: Phyrexian Arena, 2 Night's Whisper, Josu Vess.
  - Mutilate kills your own creatures too, so cast it when you're behind on board.
- **Control / counterspells / few creatures:**
  - In: 3 Duress, Seeker's Folly.
  - Out: Consuming Corruption, 1 Go for the Throat, 1 Infernal Grasp, Massacre Wurm.
- **Enchantments that matter** (Pacifism effects, Oblivion Ring, Stasis Snare / Grasp of Fate, anthems):
  - In: Withering Torment, Feed the Swarm.
  - Out: 2 Go for the Throat.
- **Hexproof / indestructible / protection threats:**
  - In: Tribute to Hunger, Consumed by Greed, Eaten Alive.
  - Out: 3 Go for the Throat.
- **White or green creature decks:**
  - In: Deathmark, plus Knight of Malice vs white.
  - Out: Consuming Corruption, plus 1 Night's Whisper.
- **Graveyard decks:**
  - In: Bojuka Bog.
  - Out: 1 Swamp.

With the owned list, use the same guide. Its sideboard has Stab, Soul-Guide Lantern (graveyard hate), Sorcerous Spyglass (names a card; that card's non-mana activated abilities, such as a planeswalker's or an equipment's, can't be used) and Vampire Spawn (vs burn) in place of the cards it already runs in the main deck.
